title: Reconstruct Itinerary
summary: Each ticket gives one directed flight.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–300 tickets. Each has two different three-letter uppercase English airport codes. A complete itinerary starting at JFK is guaranteed.
contractDetails.output-checking: Check the starting airport and exact ticket multiplicities, then compare with the lexicographically smallest complete route.

statement: Each ticket gives one directed flight. Start at JFK and assemble an airport sequence that uses each ticket exactly once, including each copy of a repeated ticket. If more than one complete itinerary is possible, return the one that comes first when the airport codes are compared from left to right.

examples.explanation: The departure from SEA continues the only route.
Taking AAA first would strand you. Visit BBB and return to JFK before taking AAA.
Both loops return to JFK. The route beginning with AAA comes first.

constraints: 1–300 tickets. Each has two different three-letter uppercase English airport codes. A complete itinerary starting at JFK is guaranteed.
hints: Conceptual: Think of tickets as edges that disappear when used.
Directional: Use Eulerian traversal. An airport with no unused departures belongs at the end of the unfinished route.
Implementation: Keep the smallest outgoing destination available. Push destinations onto a stack, append airports when they run out of departures, then reverse the result.
complexityAnalysis: O(E log E) time for sorting and O(E) auxiliary space.
